title: How to approach a public sector case
description: The first question to ask in a public sector case, how to structure it, and the trap to avoid.
hook: Public sector cases are different because the goal is rarely profit. Here is how to adjust your thinking for governments, charities and public services.
body:
The first question to ask

What does success look like for citizens and for the budget?

How to build your structure

  • Stakeholders & objectives
  • Current performance vs benchmark
  • Levers (policy, delivery, funding)
  • Implementation & risks

The trap most people fall into

Forcing a profit lens onto a social goal.

Two prompts to try

Should a city introduce a congestion charge?

Show a model structure
  • Objectives: Less traffic, cleaner air, revenue; Alternatives: parking, bus lanes, low-emission zone
  • Impact: Drivers, residents, businesses, public transport; Who gains and who loses
  • Economics: Set-up and running cost; Revenue and what it pays for
  • Implementation: Public and political support; Technology, enforcement, timing

Where to start: Objectives: the right charge depends on whether the goal is traffic, air or revenue.

The trap: Running straight to revenue without asking what the city wants to achieve.

A government wants 1 million more women in work within five years.

Show a model structure
  • Who and where: Which groups are out of work and why; Regions and sectors with the biggest gap
  • Barriers: Childcare cost and availability; Flexible hours, skills, transport
  • Levers: Childcare funding, tax and benefits; Employer incentives, training
  • Delivery: Cost per extra woman in work; How to measure progress

Where to start: Who is out of work and why: the barriers differ by group.

The trap: Listing policies without first segmenting who is out of work.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation. Practise this case type in the free casebook: every case has a worked answer.
